reasons.plausibility: Aluminum is known to promote B2 ordering and intermetallic phases in refractory BCC alloys, making the assumption of a retained single-phase BCC structure highly unlikely, especially at 20 at.% substitution.
reasons.testability: The proposed test is clear and includes quantitative rejection criteria (density reduction <10%, yield strength drop >10%, secondary phases), but the falsification condition is too lenient; a 10% strength drop is a major sacrifice of performance.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis directly addresses the density-strength trade-off with a specific composition and mechanism, but the high risk of phase instability makes it a less promising direction than exploring other lightweight alloying strategies.
